obtained.how: only the abstract, shown on the publisher's (Springer) article page above the paywall

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the Springer page's citation metadata
bibliography.note: Crossref and Springer give the title only as 'Nutrient cycling in shallow, oligotrophic Lake Kvie, Denmark' (Hydrobiologia 275(1): 267–276, February 1994, Kluwer); the entry's subtitle 'II. Effects of isoetids on the exchange of phosphorus between sediment and water' could not be checked against the title page. Volume is printed as 275/276 (a double volume); Springer lists 275, issue 1.

claims.claim: in Lake Kvie, Denmark, where isoetid lawns cover 55 % of the lake, annual P release from vegetated sediment was only 5 % of the plants' P requirement, and the authors judged isoetids 'important for keeping lakes in an oligotrophic state' (Andersen & Olsen 1994; abstract via a search summary)
claims.note: Full text paywalled. The Springer abstract carries all three items: vegetated sediments 'from the littoral zone (55% of lake area)'; 'annual P release from vegetated sediments were only 5% of the P requirements of the macrophytes'; and the closing phrase quoted. Caveat for the wording: the abstract says the littoral zone is 55 % of the lake and that its sediments were vegetated; whether isoetid lawns cover all of it is not stated. The abstract also gives SRP release < 40 µmol m⁻² d⁻¹ at all stations, release below the diffusive flux on the vegetated station (P uptake by isoetids and binding to oxidized Fe; high rhizosphere redox from root O2 release), and porewater SRP turnover 500–900 times a year. If kept, cite as '(abstract)'.
